If the fire-fighting system does not have an independent control unit and the fire detection system serves for ensuring overall control of the equipment for specific risk conditions, the serviceability of the line up to the end unit terminals shall be checked. The testing frequency of interface equipment (1) shall be as specified in the specific Standards dealing with the equipment. Tests performed in places that are not accessible due to safety reasons, due to a continuous manufacturing process or to connection of equipment to the electricty network shall be performed during planned shutdowns, and their frequency shall be at least every 18 months. The sensitivity of detectors shall be tested one year after installation and every two years thereafter. In locations where there is traceable documentation of each false alarm, the time periods between sensitivity tests may be extended. The time periods between successive

traceable documentation of each false alarm, the time periods between sensitivity tests may be extended. The time periods between successive sensitivity tests shall not be extended beyond five years and provided that the sensitivity test performed three years after installation, shows that the sensitivity of the detectors is within the specified range. In locations where there is an increasing number of false alarms compared to the previous year, the detectors shall be tested by a calibration test. In order to ensure that each smoke detector is within the marked sensitivity range, the detector shall be tested as noted in one of the following clauses: A. by a calibrated device; B by a calibrated instrument of the manufacturer; C. by means consisting of a detector – control unit, where the detector

by a calibrated instrument of the manufacturer; C. by means consisting of a detector – control unit, where the detector transmits a signal to the control unit when the sensitivity deviates from the permitted sensitivity range; D. by another means of calibration, approved by a certified laboratory. Detectors, whose sensitivity deviates from the marked sensitivity range, shall be cleaned, calibrated or replaced. Detectors that can be adjusted in the field, may be adjusted, to the desired sensitivity range. The detector sensitivity shall not be tested or measured by means of devices that supply a smoke detector or aerosol with a nonmeasured quantity or concentration. Results of the sensitivity tests shall be kept with the maintenance company. 4

He shall undergo specific training by the equipment manufacturer or by his certified representative in order to be able to perform inspection of the equipment and care for it; B3. He shall have an approval confirming his completion of the training, indicating the types of equipment that he has been certified to inspect; B4. After this period, the certified inspector shall take a refresher course for inspecting the equipment for which he was certified to care for, given by the manufacturer or by his certified representative. INTRODUCTION F i r e doors, i n s t a l l e d at openings i n p a r t i t i o n s or i n f i r e r e s i s t a n t w a l l s i n a b u i l d i n g , are intended to block the spread of f i r e through the openings f o r defined p e r i o d s . D e l a y i n g the spread of the f i r e enables people to escape from the b u i l d i n g and sometimes p r o t e c t s the p r o p e r t y i n i t . The performance of f i r e doors is dependent on a number of f a c t o r s , which can only be p a r t l y estimated and i d e n t i f i e d . F i r e r e s i s t a n c e of f i r e doors s h a l l be c l a s s i f i e d only a c c o r d i n g to the r e s u l t s of l a b o r a t o r y t e s t s of t h e i r prototypes i n an oven a c c o r d i n g to I s r a e l

c c o r d i n g to I s r a e l Standard SI 1189. The Standard does not l i m i t the use of m a t e r i a l s or s t r u c t u r a l forms for f i r e doors so as to enable t e c h n o l o g i c a l development and use of new m a t e r i a l s . 1. T h i s Standard does not determine the l o c a t ion of the v a r i o u s f i r e doors, or the method of i n s t a l l i n g them. 2• References Standards and documents r e f e r r e d to i n t h i s Standard: I s r a e l Standards: SI 1189 - F i r e r e s i s t a n c e t e s t s : Doors and s h u t t e r s . 3.
